reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of [0398] is that intention and execution can be disentangled through a Markov reward process (MRP) framework. The authors define a policy π that maps states to actions (intention), and introduce a tunable execution error parameter ε which scales the covariance of a bivariate Gaussian distribution modeling landing positions. This allows for policy evaluation under varying degrees of execution noise. As ε increases, the distribution spreads, reflecting increased uncertainty in execution. The MRP formulation enables computation of expected values V^π_ε(s) for each state s under policy π with execution error ε. The key innovation lies in treating execution error as a controllable variable, allowing separation of strategic intent from execution variability. In GSE, this translates to modeling play outcomes where intentional calls are mapped to expected point values, while execution error introduces stochasticity in those outcomes. For instance, a high-variance execution model might show that aggressive plays have lower expected value due to execution risk, whereas conservative strategies may dominate when ε is large. The framework supports both policy evaluation (MRP) and optimization (MDP) under execution uncertainty, providing a principled way to assess whether a failed play stems from poor decision-making or poor execution.
